claim_traces.claim_title: Humans only use 10% of their brains
claim_traces.claim_text: "Humans only use 10% of their brain capacity — the other 90% remains dormant and untapped."
reasoning_steps: The claim that humans only use 10% of their brain capacity is a well-known neuromyth

Modern neuroimaging techniques, such as functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and positron emission tomography (PET), show that virtually all regions of the brain are active and have designated functions
Even during sleep, all areas of the brain show some level of activity

Furthermore, evolutionary neuroscience notes that the brain consumes roughly 20% of the body's energy despite accounting for only 2% of its weight, making a 90% dormant organ an evolutionary impossibility
Scientific authorities, including Scientific American and neuroscientific organizations worldwide, have repeatedly debunked this claim.
